card.summary: Free: $0/month with Warp Agent CLI access and bring-your-own AI inference; no Warp-provided inference is included, so an agent conversation runs on the user'...

free_tier.stated: Free: $0/month with Warp Agent CLI access and bring-your-own AI inference; no Warp-provided inference is included, so an agent conversation runs on the user's own OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key, on an OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint, or on purchased pay-as-you-go usage
free_tier.notes: the agent imposes no quota on a user key or endpoint; Free-plan purchases of Warp usage are priced at a premium

record.interface_detail: the Warp Agent CLI (the `warp` binary) is an interactive terminal program; its documented flags are --api-key, --auto-approve, --resume, --set-provider-api-key, --clear-provider-api-key, --help and --version, and none is a prompt-and-exit flag, so a headless prompt mode of `warp` itself is unverified. Headless use is documented two ways: `warp` authenticates with the WARP_API_KEY environment variable on CI runners and remote servers, and the legacy Oz CLI runs a one-shot agent with `oz agent run --prompt "..."` (local) or `oz agent run-cloud` (cloud), authenticated by the same API key
record.tooling: the user installs the Warp Agent CLI with `curl -fsSL https://app.warp.dev/download/agent-cli | bash` (macOS and Linux; Windows and Homebrew installers also exist) or uses the Warp desktop app; the agent is Warp-hosted, and requests route through Warp's servers to the chosen model provider
record.chaining: the cost moves entirely to the key or endpoint: any key in inference/ that serves an OpenAI-compatible endpoint works, and Free-plan purchases of Warp usage cost a premium over paid-plan prices

limits.value: no Warp-provided inference on Free: a conversation runs only on the user's own key, a custom endpoint or purchased usage; Auto models always use Warp-provided inference, so a specific provider model must be chosen
BYOK and custom endpoints are limited to individuals and organizations of 10 or fewer employees; a larger organization needs Business or Enterprise

record.limits_note: the plan includes no inference; BYOK and custom endpoints are open only to individuals and organizations of 10 or fewer employees
record.binding_note: the plan carries no inference: capacity is whatever the user's own provider key or endpoint supplies

identity_cost.detail: the Warp Agent CLI signs in to a Warp account through a browser device-code flow, and a Google or GitHub sign-up gives Warp only the email address; no payment is taken for the $0 plan; whether a phone number is asked at sign-up is unverified: behind a sign-up

record.reliability_note: no reliability event recorded; Warp-managed model traffic is covered by zero-data-retention agreements, while traffic routed through a user key or endpoint follows that provider's retention policy
record.confidence_note: plan, BYOK, custom-endpoint and CLI statements are quoted from first-party pages read on 2026-11-02. Whether the `warp` binary has a prompt-and-exit mode is not documented on the pages read, and the legacy `oz` CLI is the documented one-shot route. Per-model token prices through a user key are the provider's and were not read.

record.notes: Models on Free are the ones the user's key or endpoint serves: OpenAI, Anthropic or Google through BYOK (the Warp catalogue lists OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and open-source models), and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as OpenRouter or LiteLLM, which must be reachable at a public URL. A Claude consumer subscription cannot back the agent; an Anthropic API key can. Cloud agent runs on Free are limited, use the Warp Agent harness only (Claude Code and Codex as cloud harnesses need a paid plan), do not use personal BYOK keys, and incur platform usage of USD 3 per agent hour.
